content.thinking:
I need to work out the causal chain for the postmortem. The root symptom is shoppers' account pages failing, tracing back to a ValueError where a summary cache entry wasn't formatted as a figure in cents, so I'm linking that to the account page error rate metric and building out the "why" chain from there.

Digging deeper, the cache format changed to amount/items during deploy P2, but the rollout paused halfway through with only 3 of 6 instances running the new code — so old readers were hitting the new format. I'm ruling out the earlier P1 deploy as the cause since the metrics window read spans back far enough to cover it, and the baseline error rate was normal throughout that period, plus no feature flag changes happened in the hour before onset.

The G46bc ClientDisconnected errors occurred well before onset, so those are just baseline noise, not a root cause signal. Tracing through the evidence, the ValueError message "is not a figure in cents" matches the old revision's reader trying to parse the new two-field entry format — confirming neither revision alone is faulty, it's the mismatch between old readers and new writers during the incomplete rollout that's causing the failures.

Both revisions shared the same cache key, so entries the new revision wrote could still reach old replicas' readers — that's how the old reader encountered the new format. So the chain starts: account pages failed for shoppers, because reading the cached spend summary raised a ValueError on the new bare-cents format.

The entry wasn't a plain cents figure because revision 696c33a (deployed per P2) changed what an entry holds, writing it as combined amount/purchase-count text instead. But the rollout was only half-complete — as of T10.1, 3 of 6 replicas were still running the old revision 5470c1a, so those old readers choked on the new two-field format.

So the root cause is straightforward: the old revision's reader treats anything that isn't a bare cents integer as an error that fails the page, and because old and new revisions shared the same cache during the partial rollout, they disagreed on entry shape. I want to keep the final step to one clean sentence tracing that mechanism back to the root cause.

For ruling out other causes, I'm checking the P1 deploy's metrics window against the baseline error rate before onset, confirming account pages rendered fine until onset, and verifying there were no flag changes by anyone other than Argus in the hour leading up to the incident — using placeholders for the actual numbers rather than hardcoding them.

I'm also noting the ClientDisconnected errors stopped before onset, so they're unrelated — just shoppers closing connections. For contributing factors, I'm thinking the rolling update stalling halfway and leaving mixed revisions sharing a cache is really part of the causal chain, but a true contributing factor is that nobody verified the new cache entry format was backward-compatible with the old revision's readers before deploying.

I'm also weighing whether the lack of paging counts as a separate contributing factor — Argus resolved things quickly, so it's unclear a human would've caught it sooner, but the instructions flag the absence of paging as a finding worth calling out on its own.

For the rollout pause, mixed-version serving is somewhat inherent to any rolling update, so I'm debating whether to fold it into the causal chain as step four or treat the stalled rollout itself as the prolonging factor rather than the root cause.

I'll frame a contributing factor around the absence of a rollout gate that halts or rolls back deployments when error rates spike — had that existed, the system would have reverted automatically at onset instead of waiting for someone to notice the alert, pointing toward an action item for adding automated rollout analysis.

For root causes, I'm noting the old revision's cache reader fails on unreadable entries, but setting that aside since it's already covered. For action items, I'm drafting one around adding a CI test that runs the previous revision's reader against entries the new revision writes to the shared cache, and considering whether a process requirement around versioned cache keys should be a separate item or folded into the existing fix.

I'm also adding items for configuring the rollout to auto-halt and roll back when error rates spike, routing high error rate alerts to an on-call page, and investigating why the rolling update paused halfway without explanation. I'm weighing whether the still-at-risk entries from the new revision still land in places the old revision reads, since the repository may still hold the problematic revision.

Pinning down the root cause: revision 696c33a changed the cache entry format from a bare cents figure to text holding both the amount and item count, but the older revision 5470c1a's reader expects only a cents figure and raises a ValueError on the new format, which fails the account page outright rather than degrading gracefully.

For the lessons that went well, I'm noting that the Investigator Agent correctly tied the onset to the 696c33a deployment and caught the mixed-revision rollout state, Argus rolled back the deployment and confirmed recovery by watching the service return below incident level, flag history was checked to rule out flag changes, and Code-Fix recognized its proposed fix alone wouldn't resolve things.

For what went wrong, nobody was paged during the incident. I'm leaving the "got lucky" section empty since the rollback resolved things through deliberate action rather than chance.

For assumptions, I'm noting the ValueError wasn't explicitly tied to a replica or revision in the logs, so I inferred it was running 5470c1a based on the error message and D1's behavior with unreadable entries; also that U1 read from main rather than 696c33a, and that cache entries are shared across revisions under the same key based on D1's behavior.

No durations need to be included, and the chain step citing T10 is instantaneous. Time to write up the final answer.

action_items.item: Add a CI test that runs the previous revision's summary cache reader against entries the new revision writes, and the reverse, for any change to a shared cache entry format.
Configure io-shop rollouts to halt and roll back automatically when the error rate rises above its baseline during the rollout.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop so that it pages the on-call engineer.
Find out why the rolling update of 696c33a stopped half-way and stayed paused.

causal_chain.step: Account page requests failed because reading the shopper's cached spend summary raised a ValueError: the cache entry '{G3714.1}' was not a figure in cents.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision 5470c1a: the metrics read between it and the onset show the service at its usual error rate of {errors_before}, and account pages rendered normally until just before the onset.
A feature flag change: the flag provider's history shows no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour before {T16.4}.
Shoppers closing the connection: those account page failures stopped before the onset.

causal_chain.step: Entries in that two-field form were in the cache because revision 696c33a, deployed at {P2.1}, changed a summary cache entry from a bare cents figure to text holding the figure and the purchase count, written as 'amount/items', under the same shopper.

A reader that expected a bare cents figure still read those entries because the rollout had stopped half-way. As of {T10.1}, {T10.2} of {T10.3} replicas ran 696c33a and {T10.5} still ran the old revision 5470c1a, with the rolling update paused and both revisions sharing the cache.
The old revision's reader raises an error on any entry that is not a bare cents figure, and that error fails the page.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A new version of the shop changed how it stores each shopper's saved spending summary, and while the update was stuck half-way, the older version still running beside it could not read the new kind of entry and failed the shopper's account page.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that tested whether the revision being replaced could read the new summary cache entry format before the change went out.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The mismatch between the new entry format and the old revision's reader would have been caught before deploy, and the change would have been held back or made readable by both revisions.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No rollout safeguard was seen that halts or rolls back a rollout when the service's error rate rises while revisions are mixed.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The rollout of 696c33a would have been rolled back as soon as errors rose, without waiting for the alert and a manual rollback.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent found that the rollout of 696c33a was paused with the old and new revisions serving side by side.
Argus read the flag provider's history, which ruled out a flag change.
The Mitigation Agent rolled back the deployment of io-shop off revision 696c33a.
The Mitigation Agent checked the service and confirmed that the rollback had worked.
Code-Fix saw that its fix would not help on its own and kept none of it, so no partial fix was merged.

went_wrong: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to the alert.

input.root_cause: Revision 696c33a changed what a summary cache entry holds, from a bare cents figure to one piece of text carrying the figure and the purchase count ('amount/items'), and wrote it where the previous revision 5470c1a, still serving alongside it, reads. 5470c1a's reader raises a ValueError on any entry that is not a figure in cents, and that error failed the account page instead of the page working the figure out again.
input.still_at_risk: Deploying revision 696c33a again while any replica still runs the old revision could make account pages fail in the same way.
